memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses then left Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord. And the Lord changed the wind to a very strong west wind, which caught up the locusts and carried them into the Red Sea. Not a locust was left anywhere in Egypt." - Exodus 10:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses prays, and God changes the wind. The same force that brought the locusts now carries them away — every last one.

Not a locust was left. God's removals are as thorough as His judgements.

Notice again that Moses prayed for the man who had just lied to him repeatedly. He had no illusions about Pharaoh, and he prayed anyway. That is a hard discipline: to keep interceding for someone whose sincerity you doubt.

Notice too where the locusts end up — the Red Sea. A small detail with a large shadow over it. That same sea will soon swallow Pharaoh's army. God is already using the water that will finish this story.

And notice the reversal of the wind. What God sends, God can turn. An east wind became a west wind at the sound of one man's prayer.

Whatever wind is blowing against you, it answers to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I willing to pray for someone I do not trust?
2. What situation do I need to ask God to turn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You govern the winds. Turn what is blowing against me, and give me grace to pray for those who have wronged me. Amen.
